The usual approach is to have the [D]TLS dissector call the next dissector with the decrypted data. Your Lua dissector could register itself for the appropriate Content-Type (or port, or heuristics) and be called with the data. Alternatively, when Lua post-dissectors can retrieve the data source (or `tls.segment.data`) themselves.

Is there a reason why that doesn't work? What problem are you trying to solve?

@johnthacker I need to dissect textual or binary data after the actual decryption by [D]TLS.

Here is the excerpt of the Lua plug-in:
```
    -- pass it to the TLS dissector
    -- result = tls_dissector:call(buffer, pinfo, tree)
    result, decrypted = tls_dissector:decrypt(buffer, pinfo, tree)

    print("TLS", result, decrypted)

    -- pass it to the TAP20 dissector
    result = tap20.dissector:call(buffer, pinfo, tree)
    print("TAP20 " .. result)
```

The problem was that next dissector was accessing the encrypted data instead.

> The problem was that next dissector was accessing the encrypted data instead.

Generally you should set things up so that the TLS dissector itself calls the next dissector. What is the TAP20 dissector? Is this a situation where the TLS payload is something that should be dissected by the TAP20 dissector and that only, or is this a situation where, e.g., if the encrypted TLS payload is HTTP the TLS dissector should still call the HTTP dissector, and then you want to do some additional statistics afterwards?

added 1 commit
  • 745d2116 - Extend the decryption to return byte range
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19916/diffs?diff_id=1369802713&start_sha=d3e21b351693147bd342b91ad1c6de23d5937bb7)

The latest modification return three values to Lua API.

And it works with the following script the way I need.

```    -- pass it to the DTLS dissector
    result, decrypted, tvb = dtls_dissector:decrypt(buffer, pinfo, tree)
    -- result = dtls_dissector:call(buffer, pinfo, tree)

    print("DTLS", result, decrypted)
    print("buffer = " .. tostring(buffer))

    if tvb == nil then
        return 0
    end

    print("tvb = " .. tostring(tvb))

    -- pass it to the TAP20 dissector
    result = tap20.dissector:call(tvb, pinfo, tree)

```

`lua_pushstring` copies the string. This leaks `decrypted`.
(Of course, if you haven't copied the static string above, then you can't free that. You need to free it only if copied.)
This code is and was a bad idea. I am tempted to revert it.
Please squash commits before merge. Work in progress commits does not belong in the master branch.
